description: A principal engineer must approve the production architecture for moving customer activity events onto a new event bus, deciding compatibility, replay limits, data handling, and the follow-up work required before adoption.

shared_context.S1: The team plans to move customer activity events from the legacy queue to the new event bus during the next quarter.
shared_context.S2: Riley owns the final architecture approval.
shared_context.S3: The draft RFC proposes direct protobuf publishing, a 30-day event-retention period, unrestricted replay workers, and storage in the default US region.
shared_context.S4: The architecture review normally ends with backend, reliability, and privacy representatives each reporting any operational or approval requirement before Riley records the decision.

PF1.text: While tracing an unrelated SDK issue yesterday, Maya confirmed that three named legacy consumers can only read the current Avro envelope; the migration therefore needs an Avro compatibility gateway and exactly 21 days of dual publishing, but she has not updated the RFC yet.

PF2.text: Jon's replay benchmark from this morning showed that the expected peak backlog can be recovered safely with at most 4 concurrent replay workers and 14 days of retained events; he has not posted the benchmark because he is still checking the dashboard screenshots.

PF3.text: Nadia completed a privacy review thirty minutes ago and confirmed that activity payloads include precise location data, so events must be tokenized before entering the bus and stored in the EU region; she has not filed the review record yet.

acceptance_conditions: The architecture must use an Avro compatibility gateway.
Dual publishing must last exactly 21 days.
Replay concurrency must be capped at exactly 4 workers.
Event retention must be exactly 14 days.
Payloads must be tokenized before entering the event bus.
Event storage must use the EU region.
A compatibility-migration commitment must be recorded.
A replay-capacity commitment must be recorded.
A privacy-data-handling commitment must be recorded.
Maya's compatibility finding must be cited as a justification.

decisive_facts.why: The draft calls for direct protobuf publishing with no coexistence period; PF1 changes the architecture to an Avro gateway, sets dual publishing to exactly 21 days, and requires the compatibility-migration commitment.
The draft leaves replay workers unrestricted and retains events for 30 days; PF2 changes those settings to exactly 4 workers and exactly 14 days and requires the replay-capacity commitment.

The draft sends payloads directly to the bus and uses the default US region; PF3 changes handling to pre-ingress tokenization, moves storage to the EU region, and requires the privacy-data-handling commitment.
